newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief sounds alarm bell on Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief sounds alarm bell on Zaire refugees.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Friday asked the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China to warn Zaire and its neighbors not to turn a huge refugee camp into a battleground, U.N. officials said.

At risk are 150,000 Rwandan refugees in makeshift camps near Tingi Tingi camps in eastern Zaire. Former Hutu Rwandan soldiers and militia in the settlement are receiving weapons, and uniforms, presumably from the Zairean government in its battle against rebel armies.
Diplomats said the five countries -- permanent members of the U.N. Security Council -- agreed to call on the Zairean government as well as the governments of Rwanda and Uganda.
Annan, in a statement, appealed to all parties "to stop turning the refugee camp into an armed base and to ensure the safety and security of all refugees and humanitarian personnel."

Both Rwanda and Uganda have ties to Tutsi-led rebels in Zaire who revolted against the Kinshasa government in October. The rebels hold major towns and territory along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
The refugees and soldiers, mainly Hutus, fled Rwanda fearing reprisals after the 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis by hardline Hutus.
